relevance_note: Family report of Blau syndrome with individual detail on the proband and her daughter, both carrying the CARD15/NOD2 variant: 'A new CARD15 E383K mutation was found only in the patients described here.'
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and located each span in the paper by matching my quoted words across the paper's tab/carriage-return/no-break-space word separators and soft-hyphen sequences (-\u00ad-), so spans carry those characters verbatim. Scope: proband (unnamed person 1; 'the proband' is a role word) and her affected daughter (rule 2 label), both carrying CARD15 E383K; five relatives (two sisters, brother, husband, other daughter) who underwent genetic investigation, did not carry the variant ('found only in the patients described here') and showed no BS symptoms; they get individual rows but no variant rows. Table 1 (literature summary by family) gives only per-family counts, which identify no individual, except the Masel (2005) row with 1 affected member in 1 generation; I gave that person one row (label 'Table 1 row 18', counting each family as one logical data row although the Markdown wraps each family over several lines) with features read from counts of 1 of 1; all other families get no rows. The Van Duist (2005) row (ref [5]) is the earlier report of this same family; its counts (joint involvement 1 of 2) disagree with this paper's text, where both proband and daughter have arthritis. Contradiction: the abstract says 'The proband, but not the daughter, complained of severe chronic bilateral uveitis', while the case text says the daughter at 13 'presented bilateral anterior uveitis'; both feature rows are emitted and the uveitis checklist item is 'not reported' for the daughter. The abstract sentence may also be read as denying glaucoma and cataracts in the daughter; I did not exclude those. The ophthalmologic examination negative at 12 is recorded as written (excludes nothing more specific). Normal chest X-ray, ECG and abdominal ultrasound are recorded as written and exclude nothing more specific. The 31 years of the proband is her age at referral in 1984, not at last evaluation, so last-evaluation age is not reported; the daughter's age at first diagnosis (about four years after onset at five) is not stated as a number. Daughter inheritance 'inherited maternal' because the paper states that her mother (the proband) carries E383K. E383K is printed only as a protein change without 'p.'; recorded in protein_hgvs_as_stated. The take-home statement that BS is 'without fever and detectable acute phase reaction' is general and was not applied to anyone.
